sensors.name: light on its right (RLIGHT) compared with 60 %
light on its left (LLIGHT) compared with 70 %
obstacle in front of its left half (LEFT)

control_flow: avoidWalls: if the right light is below 60 %, then if a wall is ahead turn left 15°, else if a wall is in front of the left half turn right 15°, else call driveInTheDark; else call driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if the left light is below 70 %, drive forward at 30 %; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if a wall is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Drive through the tunnel without hitting its walls.

decision_points.condition: the light on its right is below 60 % (it is in the dark, in a tunnel)

branches.outcome: in the dark: it looks at the obstacle sensors

decision_points.condition: in the dark, first: a wall straight ahead; second: a wall in front of its left half

branches.reason: In a tunnel the wall that comes in front of the robot is seen first by the left or by the right sensor; only a wall straight across the tunnel would be seen by the front sensor.
branches.outcome: a wall ahead: it turns left 15°
no wall ahead, a wall in front of its left half: it turns right 15°

decision_points.condition: the light on its left is below 70 %

branches.outcome: darker than 70 %: it drives forward at 30 %
no wall ahead: it follows the line

scenarios.coded_response: In the dark it drives forward at 30 %; when a wall is in front of its left half it turns right 15°, and when a wall is straight ahead it turns left 15°
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot follows a line in bright light into a tunnel; under the roof the light on its left reads below 70 % and the light on its right below 60 %, and nothing is in front of it or in front of its left half
scenarios.trigger: In the dark, a tunnel wall comes in front of it (the tunnel bends, or it drifts towards a wall)
scenarios.title: Drives through the tunnel without hitting its walls
assumptions: The robot should drive through the tunnel, not stop at its opening.
You didn't say where it should go after the tunnel.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It gets through the tunnel without hitting its walls

scenarios.coded_response: It stops while the wall is ahead
scenarios.initial_condition: In bright light, a wall is straight ahead in front of the robot
scenarios.trigger: It comes close to the wall
scenarios.title: Stops at a wall in bright light

uncertainties: You only said not to hit the tunnel walls: you didn't say what the robot should do at a wall in the light.
The program watches only the front and left obstacle sensors, so in a tunnel that bends to the left the wall comes in front of its right half, which it doesn't watch.
The left light falls below 70 % 7.5 cm inside a tunnel's roof and the right light below 60 % 10 cm inside, so it still does what it does in the light under the first centimetres of the roof.
In bright light it follows a line and circles on a plain floor, so a test has to let it follow a line into the tunnel.
